method:
python scripts/build_lessons_page_data.py            -> docs/data/lessons.json + docs/data/lessons/<date>.json
    python scripts/build_lessons_page_data.py --dump D   -> print a condensed transcript of lesson D (for reading)

Everything is on the LESSON CLOCK = the audio the lesson page plays (docs/lessons/<date>/audio/...).
Word timings come from the raw engine files, put on that clock by calibrating against the page itself:
every page line carries data-t (its first word's time on the page audio) and data-row
(<source>:row:<index into that source's Scribe words>), so offset = data-t - words[index].start, which is
constant per track (checked: spread < 0.02 s).

Sources per lesson (C:/dev/anees/data/lessons/<date>/):
  per-speaker Scribe (scribe_Medi.json / scribe_Amal.json [+ scribe_Amal_seg33.json on 09-15])  09-11 .. 09-23 except 09-18
  one diarized Scribe (scribe.json), speaker taken from the page line each word falls in         09-18
  words_labeled.json (already on the lesson clock, speaker labelled)                              08-25, 09-04, 09-05
  nothing with word timings (page has line start times only)                                       09-10 -> timing metrics null
  + data/backfill/gapfill/<date>/gapfill_<side>.json: a side whose track was empty, recovered from the mixed Meet
    recording or the person's own late-transcribed track (scripts/fill_meet_gaps.py); its lines join the turns tagged
    gap_fill + source (+ from_meet for Meet lines), its words join the timings.

Word scores run the Word Bank page's own JS (scripts/lessons_page_node.cjs) so they count exactly like it.
Grammar mistakes = the 2026-09-24 hand sweep (data/grammar-sweep-2026-09-24.json), speaking rows in an
approved bucket (docs/data/grammar-buckets.json) + unfiled rows in NEW-B18 (approved as B18).
Grammar uses = docs/data/grammar-usage.json (owned by another worker; read at build time).
Lesson types are Claude's reading of each lesson (LESSON_TYPES by hand, else the same-day reader's
data/lesson-work/lesson-types/<date>.json - LS-01), marked type_source 'claude-read'.
No paid APIs, nothing re-transcribed. Missing data -> null + a note, never a guess.

definitions.start_local: When the recording started, local time with offset. From the Meet recording's tracks.json, its folder name, or source.json. Null if none of these exist.
definitions.duration_min: Length of the lesson audio the page plays, in minutes.
definitions.type: Claude's reading of what the lesson mostly was: free-speak = conversation; review-words = practising words already taught; new-words = the tutor teaching new vocabulary (new verb pairs drilled in all tenses count here); new-grammar = the tutor teaching a rule; review-grammar = the tutor drilling rules already taught (Medi 2026-10-01: Sep 30 was an el- review). One main type; if mixed, the one with the most minutes, and type_why says so. type_source 'claude-read' = the student can correct it.
definitions.review_mode: For review lessons only: listening = the tutor says Arabic, the student gives the meaning; speaking = the student says it in Arabic; both.
definitions.words.unique: How many different Word Bank forms (a verb tense or a plural counts on its own) the student was scored on in this lesson, the lesson audit's word slips included - the same count as Progress > Vocab 'Unique words per lesson'. words.unique_rows = the same by Word Bank row.
definitions.words.right: Scored uses marked correct (same rules as the Word Bank page: its own code is run on docs/data/word-bank-evidence.json + word-bank-review.json).
definitions.words.partial: Scored uses marked partial (he got there with help) - worth half. Includes the audit's 'asked the tutor for the word' rows.
definitions.words.wrong: Scored uses marked incorrect, plus the full audit's word slips (wrong word, wrong form, English for a word she taught).
definitions.words.pct: Word score for the lesson: (right + half of partial) / all scored uses, as a percent. The Word Bank's own weighting.
definitions.grammar.uses: Times the student's Arabic exercised a scored grammar rule in this lesson, right or wrong: the uses docs/data/grammar-usage.json counted, plus every slip the tutor fixed that no counted use within 2 s pairs with (he tried the rule; the counter cannot read turns written in Latin letters). Same formula as the Grammar Console (scripts/grammar_math.py).
definitions.grammar.mistakes: Grammar slips the tutor fixed (voiced or typed) in this lesson: full audit 2026-09-26 speaking rows filed in an approved rule, minus the rows the tutor's notes take out. Includes slips in rules no counter can score (unscored_mistakes).
definitions.grammar.scored_mistakes: The slips that are in scored rules (rules with a usage counter, taught, not a sound).
definitions.grammar.unscored_mistakes: Slips in rules no counter can see his right uses of (e.g. B18): listed and counted as slips, left out of grammar.pct.
definitions.grammar.pct: Share of rule uses that were right: 1 - scored_mistakes / uses, as a percent. Never an estimate: mistakes <= uses by construction.
definitions.talk.medi_s: Seconds the student was talking: his words glued into turns (gaps under 1.2 s), turn lengths added up. Stretches the engine marked '[speaking Arabic]' count as talk.
definitions.talk.speak_pct: The student's share of the talking: medi_s / (medi_s + amal_s).
definitions.talk.listen_pct: The tutor's share of the talking (the time the student was listening to her).
definitions.fillers.count: The student's filled pauses (the technical name: filled pauses, a kind of disfluency) - uh, um, er, eh, mm, hmm, ah, and Arabic ام / امم / آآ / ممم; آه and اه only when they come mid-sentence (at the start they usually mean 'yes'). The engine drops some, so this is a floor.
definitions.fillers.per_min: Filled pauses per minute of the student's own talk time.
definitions.fillers.top: The most frequent ones, with counts.
definitions.fillers.in_turns: How many of those filled pauses the lesson page's own turns (docs/data/lessons/<date>.json) still carry. The early pages (08-25, 09-04, 09-05) were cleaned of fillers, so their turns hold almost none.
definitions.fillers.comparable: True when in_turns is at least half of count, i.e. the page transcript and the engine words agree on how much hesitation was heard. False = a different recording set-up or cleaning step: read per_min against lessons recorded the same way only (shown with '≈' on the Overview tab).
definitions.latency.median_s: Response latency: seconds from the end of the tutor's turn to the start of the student's reply, middle value. Only replies within 15 s; overlaps (he starts before she stops) are left out. A pause is not an error (rule S5) - this is a speed measure only.
definitions.latency.p75_s: Three quarters of his replies started within this many seconds.
definitions.flow.wpm: Speaking flow: Arabic words per minute inside the student's Arabic turns (a turn = words with gaps under 1.2 s; only turns with at least 2 Arabic-script words; filled pauses not counted as words). English-only turns and Latin-script transliterations are left out.
definitions.flow.n_turns: How many of his Arabic turns went into wpm.
definitions.new_words: Only words the tutor (or the student) marked new for this lesson (amal_rules kind='new'). Never guessed from the recording (hard rule 2026-09-05).
definitions.taught: New verbs: the verb pairs the tutor taught in this lesson (the student confirmed 2026-09-25). review = first taught in an earlier lesson. From the hand list TAUGHT, else the same-day reader (LS-01, data/lesson-work/lesson-types/<date>.json).
definitions.taught_words: Other words the tutor introduced as new in this lesson, read from context by the same-day reader (LS-01): shown on the lesson page, never fed to any score.
definitions.type_read_by: Who read the type: hand (LESSON_TYPES in the builder) or the same-day reader (claude -p in review_lesson.py, or an agent by hand). null = not read; the publish guard blocks.
definitions.gap_fill: Stretches where one person's side was missing and was recovered later (scripts/fill_meet_gaps.py): side, lesson-clock window, parts by source, lines added, clock offset + residual, diarization confidence. Those turns carry gap_fill: true and a source: own_track = the person's own recording transcribed late; meet_mixed = Google Meet's mixed recording, also from_meet: true - speakers there are split by the engine, not by separate microphones.

summary.headline: el- review: general statements, noun + adjective, haada / hadol + el-, and two-noun chains (idafa)

rules.title: General statements take el-: el-akel muhem = food is important
rules.pattern: el- + noun + adjective (no el-) = X is Y
bullets: Talking about something in general still uses el-: el-akel el-3arabi zaaki kteer.
Noun with el- + adjective without el- = a sentence: el-akel muhem (food is important).
Put el- on the adjective too and it becomes a label: el-akel el-muhem = the important food.

examples.line: الأكل مهم - food is important (الأكل المهم = the important food)

rules.title: haada / haadi / hadak / hadik / hadol / hadolak: the noun after them takes el-
bullets: hadol el-fasateen el-8aalyeen = those expensive dresses.
Drop the second el- and it becomes a sentence: hadol el-fasateen 8aalyeen = those dresses are expensive.

examples.line: هدول الفساتين غاليين - those dresses are expensive (take out the second ال)
haada, haadi, hadak, hadik, hadol, hadolak
hadoal el-swaat muz3ejeen - these voices are annoying
hadik el-mu8aniye aseera - that singer is short
hadoalak el-naas zaruna - those people visited us

rules.title: Noun + adjective: both get el-, or neither, or only the noun (el-walad el-3ayaan / walad 3ayaan / el-walad 3ayaan)
rules.pattern: el- + noun + el- + adjective = the X Y  |  noun + adjective = a X Y  |  el- + noun + adjective = the X is Y
bullets: a big table: no el- at all. the big table: el- on both. the table is big: el- only on the noun.
el-walad el-3ayaan = the sick boy. el-walad 3ayaan = the boy is sick.

examples.line: the big table is الطاولة الكبيرة; a big table is طاولة كبيرة
الطاولة كبيرة - the table is big

rules.title: Two nouns (idafa): el- goes only on the second noun: baab el-8urfa, dars el-3arabi
rules.pattern: noun + el- + noun  |  feminine first noun ends in -t  |  three nouns: el- only on the last
bullets: baab el-8urfa = the room's door. Its adjective comes after, with el-: baab el-8urfa el-maftoo7.

haadi goes in front without changing anything: haadi shajaret el-tuffaa7.

summary.headline: el- review: two-noun chains, adjectives after them, superlatives without el-, then awal / taani / nafs / 8eir

rules.title: Two nouns together (idafa): only the second noun gets el-, the first never does
bullets: sayyaaret el-BM = the BM car. The first noun takes no el-.
A feminine first noun ends in -t: sayyaara -> sayyaaret, mudeera -> mudiret.
A possessive ending (-i, -o, -ha) also makes the noun definite, so no el- there either: makaan shu8lo.

examples.line: sayyaaret el-BM illi - the BM car is mine
mudiret u5ti la2eemi - my sister's manager is mean
makaan shu8lo b3eed - his workplace is far
3ailet sadiqi - my friend's family

rules.title: An adjective after a possessed noun takes el-: shantet shu8li el-7amra
bullets: shantet shu8li is definite (it is mine), so its adjective is definite too: el-7amra.
Without el- it turns into a sentence: shantet shu8li 7amra = my work bag is red.
The adjective's gender shows which noun it describes: esem madrasto el-2adeem (the name) / el-2adeeme (the school).

examples.line: if it's possessed by a pronoun it's definitive, so the adjective after it should be definitive as well
shantet shu8li el-7amra - my red work bag
esem madrasto el-2adeem/e - the old name of his school / the name of his old school
tayyaaret jaari el-mit2a55ra - my neighbor's late flight

rules.title: A definite noun with adjectives: every word gets el- (el-mat3am el-Irani el-jdeed)
rules.pattern: el- + noun + el- + adjective + el- + adjective
bullets: the new Iranian restaurant = el-mat3am el-Irani el-jdeed; el- repeats on every adjective.
mufaddal (favorite) is an adjective, so it never takes a possessive ending: ma7al awa3iha el-mufaddal.

examples.line: El-mat3am el-Irani el-jdeed - the new Iranian restaurant
we consider مفضل here as an adjective, so we can't really say مفضلها
ma7al awa3iha el-mufaddal / ma7al el-awa3i el-mufadal 3indha - her favorite clothing store

rules.title: Superlatives take no el-: a7san ma7al = the best store
bullets: a7san ma7al = the best store, even though English says 'the'.
aswa2 zboon = the worst customer. aktar 7ada ba7ebbo = the person I like most.
fus7a puts el- on them; spoken Arabic does not.

examples.line: a7san ma7al = the best store
the superlative term, the best, the worst, we don't have the in them
aswa2 zboon ma beyshteir ishi - the worst customer doesn't buy anything
aktar 7ada ba7ebbo - the person I like most

rules.title: awal / aa5er / taani / 8eir before a noun never take el-; after the noun they are adjectives with el-
rules.pattern: awal + noun = first  |  awal + el- + noun = the beginning of  |  el- + noun + el-awal / el-oola = the first
bullets: awal marra = the first time. awal el-usboo3 = the beginning of the week. el-usboo3 el-awal = the first week.
oola = the feminine of awal: el-laffe el-oola = the first drive.
tani ishi = the second thing. ishi taani = something else.
nafs is the opposite: it always takes el-. nafs el-ishi = the same thing (nafs ishi means nothing).

examples.line: Actually أول never takes ال ... if you want to say it before the noun
awal marra - the first time
awal el-usboo3 - the beginning of the week (awal usboo3 / el-usboo3 el-awal = the first week)
oola = first (feminine)
awal laffe, awal el-lafe, el-laffe el-oola - first drive, beginning of the drive, the first drive
nafs el-ishi - the same thing

summary.headline: Tool words before or after a noun: awal, aa5er / a5eer, taani, 8eir, nafs, kul

rules.title: awal + noun = first; awal + el- + noun = the beginning of; after the noun it is el-awal / el-oola
rules.pattern: awal + noun = first  |  awal + el- + noun = the beginning of  |  el- + noun + el-awal / el-oola = the first
bullets: awal sa3a = first hour / the first hour. No el- in front of awal when it comes first.
awal el-sa3a = the beginning of the hour. The el- on the noun changes the meaning.
After the noun it is an adjective and matches the gender: el-saa3a el-oola, el-yoam el-awal.
oola = the feminine of awal.

examples.line: awal sa3a - the first hour
awal el-sa3a - the beginning of the hour
haadi awal sa3a fi shu8lna / haadi el-saa3a el-oowla fi shu8ulna - this is the first hour in our work
awal el-sa3a = the beginning of the hour
اليوم الأول - the first day (أول اليوم = the beginning of the day)

rules.title: taani + noun = second; noun + taani = another or second; taani never takes el- in front
rules.pattern: taani + noun = second  |  noun + taani = another / second  |  el- + noun + el-taani = the second
bullets: taani yoam = second day / the second day. yoam taani = another day (or the second).
taani el-... means nothing: there is no 'beginning of' meaning like awal el-.
Feminine after the noun: el-marra el-tanye = the second time; marra tanye = another time.

examples.line: taani = second/else/other
We can't say تاني الساعة. It doesn't mean anything.
taani saa3a = second hour / the second hour
el-masari ra7 yiju fi tani youm / youm tani - the money will come on the second day / another day
hadi tani marra ana bashufek el-yoam / hadi el-marra el-tania illi bashufek elyoam - this is the second time I see you today
bashufak marra tanye = i'll see you another time

rules.title: aa5er works like awal: aa5er + noun = last, aa5er + el- = the end of; the adjective is a5eer / a5eera
rules.pattern: aa5er + noun = last  |  aa5er + el- + noun = the end of  |  el- + noun + el-a5eer / el-a5eera = the last
bullets: aa5er marra = last time / the last time. aa5er el-marra = the end of the turn.
After the noun use a5eer (m) / a5eera (f) / a5eeraat (plural): el-marra el-a5eera.
aa5er el-ijtima3 = the end of the meeting.

examples.line: The آخر as an adjective is أخير or أخيرة - last or final
a5eer/a = last/final (adjective)
aa5er marra = last time / the last time
el-marra el-a5eera = the last time
aa5er el-ijtima3 = the end of the meeting
aa5er 3ashar da2aaye2 / el-3ashar da2aaye2 el-a5eeraat - the last ten minutes

rules.title: 8eir + noun = other / different; 8eir never takes el- in front
bullets: 8eir yoam = another day. 8eir akle = a different dish.
Only one meaning (other / different), so there is no el- version to learn.
After the noun (el-yoam el-8eir) is rare; 8eir yoam is far more common.

examples.line: 8eir = other/different
غير يوم is way, way, way more common
bashufek 8eir yoam = i'll see you another day
e7na bidna 8eir akle - we want a different dish
37na 3indna 8eir dyoof kul yoam - we have different guests every day

rules.title: nafs always takes el- after it: nafs el-ishi = the same thing
bullets: nafs = the same. The noun after it always has el-.
Never el- before nafs: el-nafs el-... is wrong.
nafs is only a tool word, never an adjective after the noun.

examples.line: نفس ... it takes ال. نفس الـ issue
the rule is نفس always takes ال after, but it never takes ال before
haad nafs el-ishi - this is the same thing
ana basoo2 nafs el-taree2 kul yom - I drive the same route every day

rules.title: kul + noun = every; kul + el- + noun = all / the whole; el-kull = everyone
rules.pattern: kul + noun = every  |  kul + el- + noun = all / the whole  |  el-kull = everyone
bullets: kul yoam = every day.
kul el-yoam = all day / the whole day.
el-kull on its own = everyone.

examples.line: كل is every, and then كل ال is like all
kul + noun = every
kul + el = all / the whole
el-kull = everyone

summary.headline: Review of el- after the toolbox words: a8lab, nafs, taani, awal, aa5er, 8eir

rules.title: a8lab and nafs go before the noun, and the noun after them takes el-
bullets: a8lab = most; nafs = the same
Never el- on a8lab or nafs itself
The noun after them always takes el- (never 'a8lab min')
No el- when the noun has a pronoun ending: a8lab wa2ti

examples.line: أغلب وقتي - most of my time
a8lab el-naas - most people
a8lab el-muwazzafeen fi ma7alli maxiciyeen - most employees in my store are Mexican
e7na bnekrah nafs el-ash5aas - we hate the same people
ana u abuy beneshte8el fi nafs el-ma7al - my dad and I work in the same store
a8lab el-3arabyeen nafs el-ishi - most Arabs are the same

rules.title: An idafa pair counts as one noun: a8lab aa5er el-usboo3, not a8lab el-aa5er
bullets: aa5er el-usboo3 (the weekend) is already a joined pair
Treat it as one noun: no extra el- after a8lab
Adding el- would break the idafa rule

examples.line: أغلب آخر الأسبوع - most weekends
a8lab aa5er el-usboo3 ru7na 3ala el-shatt - most weekends we went to the beach

rules.title: taani, awal, aa5er, kul go before the noun with no el-
bullets: Before the noun: no el- on the noun
awal yoami = the start of my day; kul yoami = my whole day
taani can be plural after a noun: s7aabek el-tanyeen

examples.line: a3tini 2amees taani - give me another shirt
7abbait taani badle - I liked the second suit
awal yoami kaan sayyi2 - the start of my day was bad
kul yoami kan beyza33el - my whole day was saddening
taani ijtimaa3 kaan nafs awal waa7ad - the second meeting was the same as the first
s7aabek el-tanyeen 8eir 3an hadoal - your other friends are different from these

rules.title: After the noun they are adjectives: el-noun el-a5ira / el-oola
bullets: aa5er before the noun; a5ir / a5ira after it
awal becomes oola (fem.) after the noun
Adjective after a definite noun takes el- too

examples.line: 7abaiti el-badle el-oola - you liked the first suit
el-kundara el-a5ira kaanat bish3a - the last shoes were ugly
يومي الأول، يومي الثاني، يومي الأخير - my first, second, last day

rules.title: 8eir before the noun = another; 8eir 3an = different from
bullets: 8eir akle = another dish (before the noun is the usual order)
8eir 3an = different from; more casual than mukhtalif 3an

examples.line: ana biddi 8eir akle - I want another dish
مختلف عن و غير عن - different from

summary.headline: The el- toolbox words used on the SAT card words: taani, awal, kul, a8lab, wa7ed after the noun

rules.title: taani after a noun with a pronoun ending takes el-: خطتك التانية
bullets: After the noun, taani is an adjective: it means 'other' (or 'second')
A noun with a pronoun ending (my, your, our) is definite, so taani takes el-
taani agrees: feminine noun -> taanye

examples.line: الفستان التاني - the other dress
خطتك التانية - your other plan
ما عندك خيار تاني - you don't have another choice
عطلة تانية - another holiday
عطلتنا التانية - our second holiday

rules.title: wa7ed / wa7de goes after the noun, as an adjective
bullets: wa7ed = one; wa7de with a feminine noun
It always comes after the noun, never before
'only' is بس, not واحد: عندي بس خيار واحد

examples.line: خطة واحدة - one plan
عندي خيار واحد - I have one choice
عندي بس خيار واحد - I only have one choice

rules.title: awal before a noun with a pronoun ending means 'the beginning of'
rules.pattern: awal + noun-i = beginning of my ...; noun-i + el-oola = my first ...
bullets: أول عطلة = the first holiday
أول عطلتي = the beginning of my holiday (idafa wins)
For 'my first' put the adjective after: عطلتي الأولى

examples.line: العطلة الأولى - the first holiday
أول عطلتي - the beginning of my holiday
أول عطلة إلي - my first holiday
راح آخد عطلتي الأولى من تلات شهور - I'm taking my first day off in three months

rules.title: kul / a8lab + el-noun, and no el- when the noun has a pronoun ending
rules.pattern: kul / a8lab + el- + noun; a8lab + noun-i
bullets: كل المصاري = all the money
أغلب مصاري = most of my money (no el-)
مصاري is plural: the verb is plural too

examples.line: كل المصاري ما راح يبسطوكي - all the money won't make you happy
أغلب مصاري - most of my money

rules.title: Proper nouns never take el-: وسط أمريكا
bullets: Countries, cities and names are already definite
So no el- after وسط or any noun before them

examples.line: وسط أمريكا - the middle of America
وسط فلسطين، وسط مصر - the middle of Palestine, of Egypt
